sources.basis: estimate: the IEA finds about 70% of fossil methane (nearly 85 Mt CH4, roughly 2.4 Gt CO2e) abatable with existing technology and about 30% (35 Mt CH4) at no net cost at 2025 prices (Global Methane Tracker 2026). Payments buy speed and verification where capital, not price, is the barrier; no-cost tons raise additionality questions, so they need jurisdiction-wide baselines
sources.label: Oil, gas and coal-mine methane abroad: results payments to producers and regulators, verified by satellite and measurement

sources.basis: sourced range: LEAF Coalition purchases jurisdictional credits, reported $10 a ton floor; Nepal's January 2026 agreement is up to 4 Mt for up to $55M (about $14 a ton); Ghana and Costa Rica (2023) over $60M. Jurisdictional accounting addresses leakage better than project credits; permanence needs buffers
sources.label: Jurisdictional forest results (national or state programs, ART-TREES style), with Indigenous and local community safeguards

sources.basis: estimate: ADB's first ETM deal (Cirebon-1, 660 MW) targets retirement in 2035 instead of 2042 and up to 30 Mt avoided over 15 years; its financial terms are undisclosed
sources.label: Early coal retirement and grid results contracts (Energy Transition Mechanism and JETP style)

sources.basis: sourced: Switzerland's bilateral purchases about $36 a ton; vendor indications $30-50. As of May 2026, 128 bilateral agreements but only five completed transfers (65,000 ITMOs): the market barely exists yet
sources.label: Article 6.2 programs: renewables, efficiency, e-mobility and industry, bilateral with corresponding adjustments

sources.basis: estimate: durable removal prices remain $100s a ton; direct air capture projected at $230-540 a ton by 2050 (ETH Zurich 2024)
sources.label: Durable removals abroad (biochar, mineral weathering, direct air capture)
